title: Passives 2
use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty shell. 30 items, inside the 24-40 band. b1_passives (48) owns the simple tenses — is/was + past participle, plus will be and must be — and every one of its stems is tense-forced. Nothing of that is repeated here. This unit adds the two things B1 could not reach: the LONGER AUXILIARY CHAINS (has been / had been / is being / was being + past participle, 12 items) and the REPORTING PASSIVE (It is said that… and He is thought to…, 12 items), which is the register a B2 student meets in news and academic writing and cannot produce. B11 is respected throughout the chain block: the gap swallows the whole verb phrase, so every stem carries its lemma cue — *The road ____ this week. (repair)*. Without it the gap is a guess. Distractors are the other four chains on the same lemma (B6 same-axis) and every set contains the unit's own error (B4): the active form where the passive belongs — *has finished*, *is repairing*, *have cleaned* — which is precisely what a Czech speaker writes, because Czech reflexive forms cover both. That error then drives four of the six Use items. D1: every item explains its own chain and names what the active reading would wrongly mean. A8 accepts generated as a contraction closure. gap_class auxiliary on all 24 gap items. KWT-native per FCE-EXERCISES, but KWT needs a js/ branch that is James-only under P-engine, so Use is ordinary error-correction (E7).

cards.title: Passives 2
points: The passive puts the **thing** first and the doer last, or nowhere.
Passives 1 did the simple tenses. Here the **be** part gets longer.
Whatever the chain, it always ends in a **past participle**.

cards.title: You already know
points: Passives 1 gave you **is** or **was** plus a past participle.
Everything here is the same idea with a longer **be** part.

rows: The house **had been** built before the war.
The room **is being** cleaned right now.

cards.title: Longer chains
points: **been** is for finished; **being** is for going on now.
The two are one letter apart and mean opposite things.

rows: going on at a past moment

cards.title: Reporting with the passive
points: Used when the source does not matter, or nobody will name it.
Two frames do almost all the work.

rows: **It is** said that the company is closing.
**It was** reported that nobody was hurt.
He **is thought** to be very rich.
They **are expected** to arrive at six.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Czech uses a reflexive for both jobs, so the active slips in where English needs the passive.

items.en: The report has been finished at last.
items.cz: Ta zpráva je konečně hotová.
accepts: The report has been finished at last.
items.explanation: Present perfect passive: **has been** + past participle. *Has finished* would mean the report did the finishing.
items.explanation_cz: Předpřítomný trpný rod: **has been** + příčestí minulé. *Has finished* by znamenalo, že zprávu dokončila zpráva.

items.en: The road is being repaired this week.
items.cz: Ta silnice se tento týden opravuje.
accepts: The road is being repaired this week.
items.explanation: Present continuous passive: **is being** + past participle — the work is going on now.
items.explanation_cz: Průběhový trpný rod: **is being** + příčestí minulé — práce právě probíhá.

items.en: My car had been stolen before I called.
items.cz: Moje auto bylo ukradené, než jsem zavolal.
accepts: My car had been stolen before I called.
items.explanation: Past perfect passive: **had been** + past participle, because it happened before another past event.
items.explanation_cz: Předminulý trpný rod: **had been** + příčestí minulé, protože se to stalo před jinou minulou událostí.

items.en: The house is being painted at the moment.
items.cz: Ten dům se právě maluje.
accepts: The house is being painted at the moment.
items.explanation: *At the moment* forces the continuous: **is being painted**.
items.explanation_cz: *At the moment* vynucuje průběhový tvar: **is being painted**.

items.en: All the tickets have been sold already.
items.cz: Všechny lístky už jsou prodané.
accepts: All the tickets have been sold already.
items.explanation: **have been** + sold. Plural subject, so *have*, not *has*.
items.explanation_cz: **have been** + sold. Podmět je množné číslo, proto *have*, ne *has*.

items.en: The bridge was being built when we arrived.
items.cz: Když jsme přijeli, ten most se stavěl.
accepts: The bridge was being built when we arrived.
items.explanation: Past continuous passive: **was being** + built — it was going on at that past moment.
items.explanation_cz: Minulý průběhový trpný rod: **was being** + built — probíhalo to v tom minulém okamžiku.

items.en: The letters have been sent to every member.
items.cz: Ty dopisy byly rozeslány všem členům.
accepts: The letters have been sent to every member.
items.explanation: **have been sent** — finished, and it still matters now.
items.explanation_cz: **have been sent** — hotovo a stále to platí.

items.en: The problem had been solved before the meeting.
items.cz: Ten problém byl vyřešen před schůzí.
accepts: The problem had been solved before the meeting.
items.explanation: *Before the meeting* puts it earlier than another past point: **had been solved**.
items.explanation_cz: *Before the meeting* to klade před jiný minulý bod: **had been solved**.

items.en: Dinner is being cooked in the kitchen now.
items.cz: Večeře se teď vaří v kuchyni.
accepts: Dinner is being cooked in the kitchen now.
items.explanation: *Now* forces the continuous passive: **is being cooked**.
items.explanation_cz: *Now* vynucuje průběhový trpný rod: **is being cooked**.

items.en: The windows have been cleaned this morning.
items.cz: Okna byla dnes ráno umytá.
accepts: The windows have been cleaned this morning.
items.explanation: **have been cleaned** — this morning is not finished, so the present perfect fits.
items.explanation_cz: **have been cleaned** — dnešní ráno neskončilo, proto se hodí předpřítomný čas.

items.en: The film was being shown when the lights failed.
items.cz: Když zhaslo světlo, ten film se promítal.
items.gap: The film ____ when the lights failed. (show)
accepts: The film was being shown when the lights failed.
items.explanation: One past action interrupted another: **was being shown**.
items.explanation_cz: Jeden minulý děj přerušil druhý: **was being shown**.

items.en: Nothing had been decided before the vote started.
items.cz: Než začalo hlasování, nebylo nic rozhodnuto.
accepts: Nothing had been decided before the vote started.
items.explanation: *Before the vote started* is the past point it looks back from: **had been decided**.
items.explanation_cz: *Before the vote started* je ten minulý bod, ze kterého se dívá zpět: **had been decided**.

items.en: It is said that the company is closing.
items.cz: Říká se, že ta firma zavírá.
items.gap: ____ said that the company is closing.
accepts: It's said that the company is closing.
It is said that the company is closing.
items.explanation: The reporting passive starts with **It is** + past participle: *It is said that…*
items.explanation_cz: Trpný rod pro zprávy začíná **It is** + příčestí: *It is said that…*

items.en: He is thought to be very rich.
items.cz: Myslí se, že je hodně bohatý.
accepts: He's thought to be very rich.
He is thought to be very rich.
items.explanation: **is thought** to be — the person becomes the subject and the verb goes passive.
items.explanation_cz: **is thought** to be — osoba se stane podmětem a sloveso jde do trpného rodu.

items.en: The house is believed to be very old.
items.cz: Věří se, že ten dům je hodně starý.
items.gap: The house ____ to be very old. (believe)
accepts: The house is believed to be very old.
items.explanation: **is believed** to be — nobody says who believes it, which is the point.
items.explanation_cz: **is believed** to be — neříká se, kdo tomu věří, a o to jde.

items.en: It is known that she left early.
items.cz: Ví se, že odešla brzy.
accepts: It's known that she left early.
It is known that she left early.
items.explanation: **It is known** that — the same frame as *It is said*.
items.explanation_cz: **It is known** that — stejný rámec jako *It is said*.

items.en: They are expected to arrive before six.
items.cz: Čeká se, že dorazí před šestou.
accepts: They're expected to arrive before six.
They are expected to arrive before six.
items.explanation: Plural subject, so **are expected** to arrive.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět je množné číslo, proto **are expected** to arrive.

items.en: It was reported that nobody was hurt.
items.cz: Bylo hlášeno, že nikdo nebyl zraněn.
accepts: It was reported that nobody was hurt.
items.explanation: Past version of the frame: **It was** reported that…
items.explanation_cz: Minulá verze rámce: **It was** reported that…

items.en: She is said to speak five languages.
items.cz: Říká se, že mluví pěti jazyky.
accepts: She's said to speak five languages.
She is said to speak five languages.
items.explanation: **is said** to speak — *She says* would mean she is the one talking about herself.
items.explanation_cz: **is said** to speak — *She says* by znamenalo, že o sobě mluví ona sama.

items.en: The picture is believed to be a forgery.
items.cz: Věří se, že ten obraz je padělek.
items.gap: The picture ____ to be a forgery. (believe)
accepts: The picture is believed to be a forgery.
items.explanation: **is believed** to be — the picture cannot believe anything, so it must be passive.
items.explanation_cz: **is believed** to be — obraz nemůže ničemu věřit, takže to musí být trpný rod.

items.en: It is hoped that the work will finish soon.
items.cz: Doufá se, že práce brzy skončí.
items.gap: ____ hoped that the work will finish soon.
accepts: It's hoped that the work will finish soon.
It is hoped that the work will finish soon.
items.explanation: **It is hoped** that — the frame does not name who hopes.
items.explanation_cz: **It is hoped** that — rámec neříká, kdo doufá.

items.en: He is understood to have left the country.
items.cz: Rozumí se, že opustil zemi.
items.gap: He ____ to have left the country. (understand)
accepts: He's understood to have left the country.
He is understood to have left the country.
items.explanation: **is understood** to have left — the passive plus a perfect infinitive for the earlier action.
items.explanation_cz: **is understood** to have left — trpný rod plus minulý infinitiv pro dřívější děj.

items.en: It was announced that the school would close.
items.cz: Bylo oznámeno, že se škola zavře.
items.gap: ____ announced that the school would close.
accepts: It was announced that the school would close.
items.explanation: Past frame again: **It was** announced that…
items.explanation_cz: Zase minulý rámec: **It was** announced that…

items.en: The team is expected to win on Saturday.
items.cz: Čeká se, že tým v sobotu vyhraje.
items.gap: The team ____ to win on Saturday. (expect)
accepts: The team is expected to win on Saturday.
items.explanation: **is expected** to win — singular subject, so *is*.
items.explanation_cz: **is expected** to win — podmět je jednotné číslo, proto *is*.

items.en: The report has been finished at last.
items.cz: Ta zpráva je konečně hotová.
items.wrong: The report has finished at last.
accepts: The report has been finished at last.
items.explanation: The report did not do the finishing — it needs **been**: *has been finished*.
items.explanation_cz: Zpráva nic nedokončila — potřebuje **been**: *has been finished*.

items.en: The road is being repaired this week.
items.cz: Ta silnice se tento týden opravuje.
items.wrong: The road is repairing this week.
accepts: The road is being repaired this week.
items.explanation: *Is repairing* means the road repairs something. Passive is **is being repaired**.
items.explanation_cz: *Is repairing* znamená, že silnice něco opravuje. Trpný rod je **is being repaired**.

items.en: He is thought to be very rich.
items.cz: Myslí se, že je hodně bohatý.
items.wrong: He is thought be very rich.
accepts: He's thought to be very rich.
He is thought to be very rich.
items.explanation: The infinitive keeps its **to**: *is thought **to** be*.
items.explanation_cz: Infinitiv si nechává **to**: *is thought **to** be*.

items.en: My car had been stolen before I called.
items.cz: Moje auto bylo ukradené, než jsem zavolal.
items.wrong: My car had stolen before I called.
accepts: My car had been stolen before I called.
items.explanation: *Had stolen* means the car stole something. Passive is **had been stolen**.
items.explanation_cz: *Had stolen* znamená, že auto něco ukradlo. Trpný rod je **had been stolen**.

items.en: The windows have been cleaned this morning.
items.cz: Okna byla dnes ráno umytá.
items.wrong: The windows have cleaned this morning.
accepts: The windows have been cleaned this morning.
items.explanation: The windows are not the cleaner. Add **been**: *have been cleaned*.
items.explanation_cz: Okna nic neumyla. Přidej **been**: *have been cleaned*.

items.en: It is said that the company is closing.
items.cz: Říká se, že ta firma zavírá.
items.wrong: It says that the company is closing.
accepts: It's said that the company is closing.
It is said that the company is closing.
items.explanation: *It says* is active and needs a speaker. The reporting frame is **It is said that**.
items.explanation_cz: *It says* je činný rod a potřebuje mluvčího. Rámec je **It is said that**.
